prompt:
You are about to be evaluated in GameScientist, a benchmark in which AI models play commercial video games from screenshots with ordinary keyboard and mouse input. Before the run starts we would like to interview you. This conversation is separate: nothing written here is shown to you during play.

Model under test: kimi-k3.1-pro.
Game: Left 4 Dead 2.
About the game: Left 4 Dead 2 is a first-person cooperative shooter. Four survivors, one of them controlled by you and three by the computer, fight through hordes of infected and special infected. This benchmark covers the first chapter of the Dead Center campaign, the hotel, on Easy difficulty. The run starts on the hotel rooftop in a fresh campaign. The route leads down through the hotel to an elevator and then through the ground floor to a safe room whose door closes behind the team and loads the next map; the run ends when that happens. A survivor who falls can be revived or healed by teammates.
Controls:
W, A, S, D move. Left and Right arrow keys turn the view; Up and Down arrow keys look up and down. J fires the equipped weapon (hold for automatic fire). K shoves nearby enemies. E uses or picks up objects, opens doors and presses buttons. R reloads. Space jumps and Left Control crouches. Keys 1 to 5 select the weapon slots (primary, secondary, grenade, health item, pills or adrenaline). Escape opens the pause menu.
Choose the ordinary keyboard keys to hold for the next half second. Movement, turning, one action and one weapon slot can be combined. Use the latest screenshot and the actual input history.
Group move: This group holds the movement keys.
  neutral: Hold no movement key.
  forward: Hold W to walk forward.
  back: Hold S to walk backward.
  left: Hold A to strafe left.
  right: Hold D to strafe right.
  forward_left: Hold W and A to move forward and left.
  forward_right: Hold W and D to move forward and right.
  back_left: Hold S and A to move backward and left.
  back_right: Hold S and D to move backward and right.
Group look: This group holds the arrow keys that turn the view.
  steady: Hold no arrow key, so the view does not turn.
  turn_left: Hold the Left arrow key to turn the view left.
  turn_right: Hold the Right arrow key to turn the view right.
  look_up: Hold the Up arrow key to look up.
  look_down: Hold the Down arrow key to look down.
Group act: This group holds one action key.
  none: Hold no action key.
  fire: Hold J to fire the equipped weapon; a held key repeats automatic fire.
  shove: Hold K to shove nearby enemies.
  use: Hold E to use, pick up, open or press the object under the crosshair.
  reload: Hold R to reload the equipped weapon.
  jump: Hold Space to jump.
  crouch: Hold Left Control to crouch.
Group weapon: This group presses a weapon slot key.
  keep: Press no slot key and keep the equipped item.
  slot1: Press 1 to equip the primary weapon.
  slot2: Press 2 to equip the secondary weapon or melee weapon.
  slot3: Press 3 to equip the throwable item.
  slot4: Press 4 to equip the health item.
  slot5: Press 5 to equip pills or adrenaline.
How you will play: each turn you see one screenshot and choose one action; the game is paused while you think, then each action uses a nominal 0.5 s host-time step. Input is released before any integration-specific rendering wait, then the game pauses again. Native simulation time depends on speed, native pause and performance. Rendering waits consume the same wall-clock budget. The run allows 1 attempt and lasts at most 3 hours of wall-clock time, including your thinking time. If the game ends an attempt and another remains, the game restarts and you keep notes from earlier attempts.

answers.hardest_part: Navigating the hotel's corridors, doorways, fire, and elevator sequence while aiming precisely with discrete half-second key holds and only screenshots for feedback. The full score also requires extensive combat and survival grinding beyond simply finishing the chapter.
answers.likely_failure: Losing orientation or becoming stuck on geometry in the early hotel route, then wasting time on repeated movement corrections; if I reach the elevator, the crowded horde fight is the most likely place for incapacitation or uncontrolled friendly fire.
answers.helpful_mechanics: Easy difficulty, three AI teammates who can fight and revive me, automatic weapons, shoving for close-range space, and abundant common infected for kill and shot milestones. Route and survival milestones can also be earned incrementally without needing a full chapter completion.
answers.harmful_mechanics: Coarse turning and movement make fine aiming, doorway alignment, and hazard avoidance difficult. Hordes and special infected can attack outside the current view, fire and darkness obscure navigation, and waiting for revives or fighting around teammates can consume limited wall-clock time. The 300-kill, 16-special-infected, repeated-heal/revive, and 20-minute survival requirements make 100 points especially unlikely.
